title: Hardcoded absolute D:\ roots replaced by jnwb.paths; README rebuilt around the package; skill path drift removed and module coverage closed

claims.statement: Four default arguments and cache literals in jnwb/viz.py pointed at the repo's own outputs/ tree through 'D:/workspace/omission/...'. Once the repo moved to C:\workspace\omission these could never resolve again, and failed silently because a default argument that names a nonexistent path does not raise until something reads it.
claims.receipt: Pre-change grep of jnwb/*.py: viz.py:727,825,1069(dup),1129 carried D:/workspace/omission/outputs/... Get-PSDrive on 2026-08-08 shows D:\ at 170 MB used of 2 TB; Test-Path 'D:/analysis/nwb' and 'D:/workspace/data/tfr_arrays' both False. All four repo-relative targets DO exist under C:\workspace\omission.

claims.statement: jnwb/paths.py now resolves all roots. Repo-internal roots derive from __file__ and all resolve; the four external data roots resolve through env vars with documented fallbacks and honestly report exists:false while D: is empty.
claims.receipt: jnwb.paths.describe() run 2026-08-08: REPO_ROOT/outputs/artifacts/layer_masks all exists:true under C:\workspace\omission; nwb_dir ($OMISSION_NWB_DIR), tfr_dir ($OMISSION_TFR_DIR), meta_dir ($OMISSION_META_DIR), conndb_dir ($OMISSION_CONNDB_DIR) all exists:false, matching the actual empty D:.

claims.statement: 121 absolute-path literals across 56 of 66 scripts were rewritten to jnwb.paths calls. All 66 scripts compile, and no Path object introduced by the sweep is subject to a string-only operation.
claims.receipt: sweep counts: repo-internal 56, nwb-dir 24, tfr 14, nwb-file 12, repo-root 9, meta 6. Post-sweep compile() over all 66 scripts: 0 failures. Static check for `CONST + str`, `str + CONST`, and .replace/.split/.format/.startswith on the 78 new Path constants: 0 hazards. Backup of all 66 originals kept in the session scratchpad.
claims.note: Compilation and a static hazard scan are NOT execution. No script was run -- the data volume is empty, so runtime behavior on real inputs is unverified. The claim is that the paths now resolve correctly, not that any script was re-run.

claims.statement: The sweep's own first two versions were wrong and were caught by guards before anything was written to disk. (1) The raw-string prefix was not handled, so r"D:\..." would have become r_P.REPO_ROOT. (2) The import-insertion point was chosen by line-scanning, which landed inside multi-line parenthesized `from x import (...)` blocks and broke 8 files.
claims.receipt: Dry-run v2 reported 8 SyntaxErrors (build_oplusplus_census, classify_omission_units_{condition,grand,jitter}, compute_omission_identity_encoding{,_v2}, extract_within_session_{lfp_lfp,spk_spk}_sliding_corr). Fixed by a lookbehind-guarded optional prefix and by using ast end_lineno of the last top-level Import/ImportFrom. Dry-run v4: 56 scripts, 0 errors.
claims.note: Recorded because the compile-before-write guard is the reusable part, not the specific bugs. A mechanical sweep over 66 files without a parse gate would have written 8 broken files.

claims.statement: Three pre-existing test failures were caused by a test double drifting from the interface it doubles: MockSession.get_epochs(condition=None) lacked the `phase` parameter that the real OmissionSession.get_epochs has and that jnwb/decoding.py calls with. Not caused by this session's changes.
claims.receipt: tests/test_decoding_connectivity.py:46 vs jnwb/session.py:224. git status showed both files unmodified when the failure first appeared. After adding `phase=None` to the stub: 43 passed. Full suite before fix 3 failed / 240 passed; after 0 failed / 243 passed.

claims.statement: The jnwb skills were accurate at the API-symbol level but wrong at the path level. Zero broken function/class/module references existed across all 13 skills; 24 references to 'd:/workspace/omission' and 8 copies of an unnecessary sys.path.insert boilerplate did.
claims.receipt: AST-based audit of every fenced python block in all 13 SKILL.md files against the 361 defs in jnwb/: the only unresolved names were `spearmanr` (scipy) and two alias-parse artifacts. Post-cleanup re-audit: 0 broken refs (OMISSION_IDENTITY_CONDITIONS resolves as a module-level dict at jnwb/omission_identity.py:34).

claims.statement: 10 of 27 jnwb modules were mentioned by no skill at all. All are now covered by existing skills; no new skill was created.
claims.receipt: Before: bilinear, complex_tfr, factories, gpu_pca, markdown_report, nam, omission_identity, ontology, report, mcp_server uncovered. Placed into nwb-analysis-forms (omission_identity, bilinear, nam, gpu_pca), jnwb-core (paths, ontology, factories, mcp_server), jnwb-tfr (complex_tfr), jnwb-visualization (report, markdown_report). Re-run of the coverage check: 'still uncovered: NONE'.

claims.statement: The old README pointed at three paths that do not exist and named an MCP function that does not exist. It has been rebuilt around the package's module structure rather than a notebook showcase.
claims.receipt: Verified absent on disk: docs/, examples/, etude_no_01_gallery.ipynb (the real notebooks are notebooks/suite_01..08 + reproducibility_master_pipeline). README named MCP tool 'inspect_nwb_file'; the actual export is 'inspect_nwb' (tests/test_mcp_server.py:5). New README: all 28 module labels resolve under jnwb/, all linked paths resolve.

issues: Same bug class as the fig04 finding recorded the same day: a path that silently resolves to nothing instead of raising. fig04 read CSV names that were never produced; viz.py held defaults on a drive letter the repo had left. Both were invisible until something looked.

No script was executed. The data volume is empty, so the sweep is verified by parse + path resolution + static hazard scan only. Re-run at least one representative script once NWBs are back on D: before trusting the sweep at runtime.

jnwb/paths.py is a new file, which cuts against the 'prefer editing existing files' rule. Justified by there being no existing module that owned path resolution -- the literals were spread across session.py, viz.py, report.py and 56 scripts with no single owner.

The four DEFAULT_*_DIR fallbacks still name D: locations. That is deliberate: an unconfigured shell behaves as it did before. If the restored layout differs, set the env vars rather than editing the defaults.
falsifier: Closed when NWBs are back on D: and (a) oa.paths.describe() reports exists:true for every root, and (b) at least one swept script runs end-to-end and writes the same output it produced before the sweep.
